text:
Simone: Heads-up — platform telemetry review. We still have inconsistent span names for LLM requests across services. Some places use `llm.request` + attributes, others use `completion/<model>` as span.name. Need agreement before we wire exporters to long-term storage.

Kevin: +1, this makes dashboards a mess. My vote: keep span.name generic (llm.request) and move model+route into attributes. Easier to query for aggregates.

Maria: leaning the other way — having the first segment of span.name be the operation (`generate`, `embed`, `rank`) helps top-level dashboards. Example: `generate.text` vs `embed.vector`.

Raj: hybrid option? span.name = "llm.<op>" (e.g., "llm.generate") and attributes: `llm.model.name`, `llm.model.version`, `llm.tokens.prompt`, `llm.tokens.completion`, `llm.kv_cache.hit` (bool), `routing.policy` (string), `quota.bucket` (string). That gives both groupability and stable root.

Alice: Agree with Raj. Also add `llm.request.size_bytes` and `llm.request.input_charset` for different clients. For cache metrics we want `kv_cache.hits` & `kv_cache.lookups` as int attrs when available.

Kevin: Can we standardize attribute names to dot-separated nouns and avoid vendor prefixes? e.g., `llm.kv_cache.hit` vs `kv_cache.hit` — prefer `llm.kv_cache.hit` to namespace.

Maria: Question on span duration semantics — should span cover whole routing (including retries/fallbacks) or just single model RPC? We have traces where a request spawns two model spans (primary + fallback). Need consistent parent/child pattern so Console shows retries.

Raj: Proposed pattern: root span `llm.request` with attrs describing route + client; child spans per model call: names `llm.model_call` with attrs `llm.model.name`, `llm.model.variant`, `llm.model.latency_ms`, `llm.kv_cache.hit` (on that call). Root attribute `llm.request.outcome` = success|fallback|error.

Simone: That's solid. We should also record token counts at both levels: request-level totals and per-model contribution. E.g., root `llm.tokens.prompt_total` & `llm.tokens.generated_total`, child `llm.tokens.generated`.

Alice: Exporters note: ops wants OTLP->collector->metrics DB for long retention (12 months) but traces shorter (90d). We need to flag per-span which exporter stream it's emitted to. Maybe `telemetry.export.batch` or add `export_hint: traces|metrics|both`?

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: collector config PR #412 shipping tomorrow.

Kevin: For sampling, we should sample traces based on route sensitivity and token cost. E.g., sample 100% for routes with quota.bucket=enterprise, 1% for low-cost embed routes. We can add attr `sampling.reason` to capture why a trace was kept.

Maria: UX ask: Console wants a single drill-down: top table keyed by `llm.model.name` with columns (avg latency, p95, tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit_rate). With Raj's child spans we can compute kv_cache_hit_rate from child attrs.

Simone: Decision proposal (vote): adopt root span name `llm.request`, child `llm.model_call`; attributes namespace `llm.*` per Raj/Alice; add `telemetry.export_hint` and `sampling.reason`; store traces 90d, high-value route traces 365d via tag `telemetry.retention=long`.

Kevin: +1

Maria: +1 (prefer keeping op in child span but I'm okay)

Raj: +1

Alice: +1

Simone: OK merged — I'll draft an RFC with examples and attr list. Quick sample to put in RFC: ```json
{
  "span.name": "llm.request",
  "attributes": {
    "llm.operation": "generate",
    "llm.model.name": "redwood-7b",
    "llm.model.version": "v1.2",
    "llm.tokens.prompt_total": "42",
    "llm.tokens.generated_total": "312",
    "llm.kv_cache.hits": "7",
    "routing.policy": "latency-first",
    "quota.bucket": "standard",
    "telemetry.export_hint": "both",
    "telemetry.retention": "90d"
  }
}
```

Simone: Thanks — RFC draft in #rfc later today. If anyone has specific queries they'd like to be cheap in Console (group-by model, by route, by kv cache hit) add them as comments on the RFC. :pray:

dev-bot: Reminder: please add owners + tests for attr names to the RFC.

Simone: noted; closing this quick sync. Will ping when RFC is up.
